answer: A Sybil-resistance design is capacity-bonded admission: each new validator posts a bond sized as a multiple of the median bandwidth and storage footprint secured by existing participants, re-measured at a delta checkpoint each epoch. An attacker minting fake identities pays the full footprint cost per identity, so Sybil costs scale linearly with fleet size. The bond sits in escrow until the identity stays honestly live for a reward cycle; even at the nadir of prices the capital cannot be redeployed, making farming capital-inefficient. Each admission is sealed with an opal-stamped beacon entry.
